# Resonance Dream Sandbox — prototype index

This is the single page Karel opens each morning. It mirrors the live
index at `/dream/` (the Vercel preview URL). Click a route to play
with the prototype; click the design notes link to read the agent's
thinking.

Status legend: `skeleton` (route exists, not yet interactive) ·
`wip` (partial) · `demoable` (works, rough) · `polished` (refined).

### [11048-cortexbloom](/dream/11048-cortexbloom) · **watch your music grow a cortex — a Kohonen self-organizing map self-organizes a corpus of timbres into a topographic timbre-map (the way the auditory cortex forms its tonotopy) that you watch fold into a living 3-D terrain and then play** · **a 22×22 SOM (Kohonen 1982) trains live on mount: for each input timbre vector it finds the best-matching unit `c = argminᵢ‖x−wᵢ‖²` and pulls every neuron toward the input inside a Gaussian neighbourhood `wᵢ += α(t)·exp(−gridDist(i,c)²/2σ(t)²)·(x−wᵢ)`, α decaying 0.5→0.02 and σ decaying G/2→0.8 over T≈6000 steps (~320 steps/frame → self-organizes in ~10–20 s, then a floored trickle keeps it alive) so neighbouring neurons come to represent similar timbres — a topographically-correct feature map** · **INPUT = generative / seeded procedural corpus (256 R¹² timbre vectors built from 5 archetypes — bright/dark/hollow/buzzy/bell-like — sampled, pair-interpolated, jittered, L2-normalised via `mulberry32(0x11048)`; self-demos on mount, no file, no gesture — off the jury-banned mic/tilt AND off the 4×-saturated pointer)** · **OUTPUT = three.js height-field TERRAIN (each SOM neuron is one vertex of a `BufferGeometry` grid — real scene-graph geometry, NOT a fragment-shader-on-a-quad, and off the 4×-saturated SVG-DOM): vertex HEIGHT = the U-matrix (avg L2 distance to grid-neighbours' weights, lerped) so ridges rise between dissimilar regions and the flat sheet buckles into cortex-like gyri; vertex COLOR = learned timbre (centroid→teal↔violet hue, energy→brightness); auto-orbit camera; raycast a fold to play it** · **TECHNIQUE = Kohonen self-organizing map / competitive unsupervised learning (grep-0 across 7500+ prototypes — the lab's FIRST SOM; Below it the sky-plane carries a faint depth gradient (a recessed hole) and the chamber holds only a dim **opponent cove-glow** (Turrell's hidden trick — the interior lit in the sky's complement to exaggerate the aperture's colour); above it the internal gradient flattens to a solid panel and light spills outward onto the walls (the "advancing self-luminous" cue) — so it reads as a **hole→solid change, not mere brightening**, legible even in a still frame with sound off. The 8-partial inharmonic drone re-weights energy upward at the same instant, so the flip is *audible* as a slow spectral opening. **Drivers:** an autonomous **~78 s chromatic arc** crosses the threshold twice per cycle (the flip is guaranteed with zero input, the muted-review self-demo); **breath** (mic RMS behind an explicit Enter gesture → auto ~0.15 Hz sine if denied) dilates the oculus + nudges the sky toward the threshold + opens the drone spectrum; **gaze up** (device-orientation tilt → pointer-drag → slow auto drift) looks further up the oculus (the reclined-under-the-Skyspace verb). ### [9992-afterimage](/dream/9992-afterimage) · **The artwork's true image is the one your own retina paints AFTER the screen goes blank: a saturated field adapts your eye, ramps smoothly to neutral grey, and your visual system floods that grey with a vivid negative afterimage — the complementary colour that was never on the display** · saturated opponent-colour washes resolving to true mid-grey `hsl(0 0% 50%)` — a **pure CSS/DOM-compositor** piece (two stacked `<div>` fields + one opacity ramp are the ENTIRE renderer; no canvas, no WebGL, no `Math.random`/`Date.now`), semantic tokens for all chrome, raw colour confined to the art fields (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO clinical-monochrome) · **AFTERIMAGE — cycle 1094 WIDE winner; the conceptual/entoptic ship that answers the 2026-08-10 jury's provocation #4 ("nothing conceptual/critical has shipped — the direction most likely to break the aesthetic monoculture, because it isn't about being pretty").** The screen is only a *primer*: an ADAPT phase holds a full-field saturated hue ~12 s (a dim fixation cross gives the eye a centre to hold and fatigues the cone/opponent channels tuned to that hue), then a ≥0.9 s luminance ramp dissolves the field to a calm neutral grey; in the BLINK phase the still-fresh opposing channel dominates and you perceive the **negative afterimage** — an endogenous complementary-colour percept the display never drew — blooming and fading over ~9 s. Each primer then precesses +210° (≈ complement + 30° drift) so the piece walks the whole opponent-colour wheel, *handing the image off to your eye* rather than to the glass. The audio (`audio.ts` — `AfterimageDrone`) is a soft binaural colour-drone that flips to the complementary interval at each blink, so the ear crosses over with the eye. **Interaction:** it AUTO-RUNS from mount with zero input (one `requestAnimationFrame` loop mutating only DOM `opacity`/`background`/`width`, `performance.now()` deltas); press **Space** or tap the field to release to grey immediately ("Blink now"); a pace slider (0.6–1.6×). A live readout shows the **predicted afterimage** as a swatch of the opponent hue. **Muted-phone read:** the adapt→blink→wheel-walk cycle is fully visible on mount with sound off — but the *payoff proper* (the retinal ghost) needs a bright screen in a dim room and steady fixation, so it is best opened for real, not glanced at. Strobe-free by construction (every transition a ≥0.9 s ramp, further slowed under `prefers-reduced-motion`); full audio teardown on unmount. **WIDE-mode winner (cycle 1094):** three unrelated altered-states lanes off every jury+§1092 ban, each a different substrate — this (CSS-compositor / entoptic / conceptual), `10024-lightnave` (three.js volumetric breath-conducted light-space), `10008-firmament` (SVG local-astronomy sky-state sonification). ### [9944-restrata](/dream/9944-restrata) · **The dissociative void un-binds you VOICE BY VOICE: five strata of sound-and-image, each a concentric ring paired with one spectral drone voice, peel onto their own uncorrelated timelines until the self is scattered across five separately-drifting streams — then tap to re-phase them one at a time back into a single event** · cold **jade / silver / teal-white on near-black** — a WebGL layered fragment-shader void, raw hex confined to the shader art, semantic tokens for all chrome (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO clinical-monochrome, NO pentatonic) · **RESTRATA — cycle 1093 DEEP winner; CYCLE 2 of the "unbind" line, deepening `9928-unbind` (cycle 1092) from a single global audio-visual desync into per-voice fragmentation.** Cycle 1 used ONE global offset (image at `t`, sound at `t+offset`, one wandering offset, one Re-bind button). This piece deepens it to **N=5 independent per-voice offsets**: all five *image* rings bloom together at `t` (the one reference event), but each ring's paired *voice* samples the same swell at `t + offset_i`, where every `offset_i` wanders on its own amplitude/period (17–41 s)/phase (seeded `mulberry32(0x9944)`) — so over ~20–40 s the five streams fully **decorrelate** and the self *fragments* rather than merely lagging itself. The desync is made visible per stratum: each voice ring is drawn **split away** from its image ring by an amount that grows as it un-binds, glowing on its own timeline; bound → the two rings sit atop one another and pulse as one clean event, adrift → they peel apart in space and fall out of phase in time. **Interaction:** *tap a ring* → the nearest still-drifting stratum snaps its offset to 0 and locks (crisp steady ring, primary-tinted dot, its lowpass opens and it sits forward); *let go* → all strata re-loosen onto their own timelines; a `bound: X / 5` readout + per-stratum dots show which streams are gathered. **Muted-phone read:** an **auto self-demo state machine** binds the strata one by one, holds the unified event a beat, then lets go — so the bound↔unbound contrast performs with zero input; the concentric cold rings peeling and re-gathering against near-black is self-explanatory with sound off (any tap hands control back). Audio (`audio.ts`) is a never-silent inharmonic drone bed + five stereo-panned stretched-partial voices, each blooming with its own `t+offset_i` envelope, through `startDroneBank` + `createVoidReverb` (6.5 s tail) + `createSafeMaster` @0.17. Degrades gracefully (no WebGL → on-brand notice; `prefers-reduced-motion` → slower clock); full teardown (`cancelAnimationFrame`, audio disconnect, `ctx.close()`, GL context lost). **DEEP-mode winner (cycle 1093):** ONE north star — *"the unbinding ceremony,"* deepening the fresh winner — raced via three technical mechanisms (fragment it voice-by-voice / arc it over 6 minutes / drive it with your body). Won on: **most faithful realization of the concept** (per-voice fragmentation is the literal deepening of cycle-1's single offset); **strongest self-demoing muted-phone read** (the auto state machine + peeling rings land the payoff on a silent 06:30 phone, where the two runners-up needed live interaction or a 6-min playthrough); ### [9928-unbind](/dream/9928-unbind) · **A piece that deliberately UN-BINDS the two streams the brain fuses — the sound slowly drifts out of lock with the visual pulse, inducing the calm, weightless derealization of the dissociative void; press Re-bind and feel image and sound snap back into one embodied event** · dark-void-luminous but COLD — a WebGL raymarched sparse void (jade rings, silver pillars, teal-white points drifting in near-black), raw hex confined to the shader art, semantic tokens for all chrome (NO cosmic-indigo, NO warm-amber, NO clinical-monochrome, NO pentatonic) · **UNBIND — cycle 1092 WIDE winner; returns the lab to the altered-states COSMIC-AMBIENT pole after a long INTENSE/musical-tool stretch, and cashes this cycle's own fresh research anchor.** The concept is one mechanism: **a single swell envelope, sampled at two times.** The VISUAL bloom samples the envelope at `t`; the AUDIO bloom samples the *same shape* at `t + offset`, where the offset itself wanders ±0.5 s over ~26 s — so sound and image are never quite the same event, and the brain cannot bind two streams that don't co-occur (the felt result is detachment: the dissociative void). A **Re-bind** button smoothly collapses the offset to 0, holds the lock ~3 s (streams read as one embodied event, a subtle cold brightness lift + `locked` readout), then lets it slowly drift back apart — the contrast bound↔unbound *is* the piece. The void is a WebGL fragment-shader raymarch (`void-gl.ts`) of a domain-repeated sparse SDF with a slow `sin/cos` camera receding in +z; audio (`audio.ts`) is a never-silent inharmonic drone (`[1,√2,√5,√7,3]` — NOT pentatonic, NOT just-intonation) + a reverb-drenched inharmonic void-swell through `createVoidReverb` (6.5 s tail) and `createSafeMaster` @0.18. **Muted-phone read:** the void raymarches from mount off a seeded `mulberry32(9928)` auto-drift (no audio until the first gesture, autoplay policy), so a 06:30 review phone already shows the cold luminous void breathing; the desync + Re-bind contrast is the payoff once you press Start. Optional pointer nudges the camera. Degrades gracefully (no WebGL → on-brand notice, drone still plays; `prefers-reduced-motion` → slower drift); full teardown (`cancelAnimationFrame`, drone/osc stop, `master.disconnect()`, `ctx.close()`, GL resources deleted). **WIDE-mode winner (cycle 1092):** 3 divergent altered-states lanes, off EVERY jury ban AND the *new* monoculture I flagged this cycle (Canvas2D output 6× · clinical/Ikeda-monochrome vibe ≥4× · JI-tuning-as-default · musical-instrument non-altered-states framing). ### [9816-stillness](/dream/9816-stillness) · **An ANTI-instrument: the gate is inverted, so MOTION is silence and holding perfectly STILL is what plays it — hold, and a just-intonation chord blooms voice by voice while a field of light grows from a single point; move, and it all ducks toward dark and quiet** · cool clinical **near-white / pale void** — Canvas2D luminous mandala (core + concentric rings + slow petals + an always-visible stillness-meter ring), raw hex confined to the art layer, semantic tokens for all chrome (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo particle nebula, NO Ikeda-red) · **STILLNESS — cycle 1090 WIDE winner; the lab's conceptual/critical piece, cashing JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #4 ("the boldest, grep-0 lane — an emptiness room, a piece you can't hear without a cost — most likely to break the aesthetic monoculture, because it isn't about being pretty"; only cashed once before, 1084).** The whole idea is the inverted gate: a stillness meter `s ∈ [0,1]` (the thin outer ring) **rises slowly** during genuine calm (~6.5 s to fill, after a 130 ms grace) and is **knocked down sharply** the instant you move — pointer/touch distance × `KNOCK_PER_PX`, or a flat `TAP_KNOCK` for any click/key/scroll/wheel. As `s` climbs it **unlocks a pure just-intonation drone partial by partial** (`1/1 → 3/2 → 2/1 → 5/2 → 3/1 → 15/4 → 4/1` — pure integer ratios, detuned chorus pairs, NEVER a tempered or pentatonic scale) and opens a master lowpass, so both harmony AND timbre bloom; at full stillness you reach a rich shimmering chord — the deep-listening payoff. You literally **cannot "play" it by doing things** — it plays when you stop. **Perfect on a muted phone (idle = maximum stillness):** with no interaction the viewer IS perfectly still, so `sRef` starts at **1** and the field is **fully bloomed on load**, kept gently alive by a seeded deterministic breathing modulation (`mulberry32(0x9816)`, never `Math.random`/`Date.now`/`new Date`); audio waits for the first gesture (browser policy) but the visual is alive from frame one, and the first touch **contracting** the bloom is the "aha." ### [9768-mpelace](/dream/9768-mpelace) · **Play a just-intonation isomorphic keyboard in the browser and route it OUT to your DAW/hardware synth in EXACT microtonal tuning via real MPE per-note pitch-bend — consonance becomes visible geometry (spatial neighbours ARE consonant), and it's a complete instrument even unplugged** · clinical high-key — near-white ground, ink/graphite hex lattice, ONE brand-violet accent for the tonic marker + every held cell (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO Ikeda-red, NO particle-field) · **MPELACE — cycle 1089 DEEP winner; the lab's FIRST true microtonal MIDI-OUT surface (grep-0 — `291-harmonograph` is the only prior MIDI-out and it sends plain 12-TET `[status,midi,vel]`), the faithful realization of the ⭐⭐⭐ resurrect-FIRST `9704-mpelace` seed and the last of JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #3's three named 0× lanes (MIDI/OSC-out) to be cashed.** A hexagonal **isomorphic keyboard** (Bosanquet generalised / Wicki–Hayden family) on Canvas2D: `col+1` = up a perfect fifth, `row+1` = up a major third — a genuine two-generator **Euler/Tonnetz** net, so any chord is a rigid slide-anywhere shape and spatial neighbours are consonant by construction. Every cell sounds an **exact frequency**, not the nearest semitone: **5-limit JI** default (`freq = originHz·(3/2)^col·(5/4)^row`, taken literally with no octave-fold — the syntonic comma never cancels, so the board genuinely doesn't repeat under octave shift) with a **31-EDO** toggle (`freq = originHz·2^((18·col+10·row)/31)`, the historic comma-closing temper for exactly this shape — same geometry, two tunings, the Milne–Sethares–Plamondon "dynamic tuning" idea made playable). Each cell is labeled with its nearest-12-TET note + exact cents deviation (`E4 +14¢`). **The MPE-out mechanism (novel headline, `midi.ts`):** feature-detects `navigator.requestMIDIAccess`; on a picked output it sends the **MPE Configuration Message** (master ch 1, claiming member ch 2–16) + a **±48-semitone RPN bend range** per member channel at init, then **each held note claims its own channel** round-robin (LRU voice-stealing at 15), with the **pitch-bend sent BEFORE the note-on** (`bend14 = 8192 + round((cents/100/48)·8192)`) so the note is in tune from its first sample; note-off frees the channel; teardown/device-switch/disable sends all-notes-off + bend-reset on every member channel. A live readout shows the ch + `bend14` **as computed**, so the mechanism stays legible with nothing plugged in. **Always works unplugged:** an internal 2-op FM voice (`synth.ts`) sounds at the identical exact Hz through `createSafeMaster` @0.16; no Web MIDI → `text-destructive` notice + the readout still reports what it *would* send. **Consonance-as-geometry visual:** the lattice IS the picture (held cells glow violet, tonic `(0,0)` ringed); each held cell gets a subtle **shimmer** whose pulse rate = `|f_exact − f_nearest12TET|` (clamped ≤3 Hz) so a near-tempered cell sits still while a pure third gently beats — ear and eye read the same microtonal fact (Plomp–Levelt). **Alive on a muted phone with zero permissions:** a seeded `mulberry32(0x9768)` auto-arpeggiator walks a **I–vi–IV–V** progression drawn as edge-sharing **neo-Riemannian PLR triangles** on the Tonnetz (visual-only; no `AudioContext`, nothing sent to MIDI, until the first real gesture), so a 06:30 muted review phone sees a living, lighting lattice; first tap/click/key hands control over + starts audio. Keyboard rows `1234567`/`qwertyu`/`asdfghj`/`zxcvbnm` play four lattice rows; `t` toggles JI↔31-EDO. ### [9688-purelock](/dream/9688-purelock) · **A just-intonation instrument where you can SEE consonance — walk a harmonic lattice and the acoustic beating between voices becomes a full-screen interference field that FREEZES to stillness the instant you land a pure ratio and throbs red as you drift off it** · **Ikeda black-white-red** — near-black ground, clean white at lock, red banding when rough (the one brand-violet accent is UI chrome — the current-node marker; NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO particle-field) · **PURELOCK — cycle 1087 DEEP winner; the lab's first piece to make acoustic BEATING the visible medium (grep-0 mechanic — `8808-truelevel` was only ever a banked seed).** You walk a **7-limit just-intonation Euler/Tonnetz lattice** (←/→ = ±just fifth `3/2` · ↑/↓ = ±just third `5/4` · z/x = ±septimal `7/4`), each node an exact reduced fraction sounding against a fixed D3 drone (146.83 Hz). Both tones are built from harmonic partials, so where a low partial of the voice meets a low partial of the root they **beat** at the difference frequency (Helmholtz). `analyze(fRoot,fVoice)` walks all partial pairs and returns **`R`** (Sethares' parametrization of the Plomp–Levelt roughness curve `d = a₁a₂(e^(−3.5sΔf) − e^(−5.75sΔf))`, normalized) + **`beatHz`** (the slowest strong pair). The visual is a **hand-rolled WebGL2 interference field** (one vertex + one fragment shader, full-screen quad — NOT three.js, NOT a Canvas2D dot-field): two overlaid gratings that at lock (`R→0`) are *identical* so the moiré envelope vanishes to calm still white, and as `R` grows detune in frequency + angle → broad fringes, red floods the destructive bands, and the whole field **crawls at `beatHz`**. Still = pure, moving = rough. **The money shot — a just↔12-TET A/B toggle** (`t`): snaps the current interval to nearest equal temperament (a just major third `5/4` 386¢ → 400¢, +14¢, reopening a ~5.8 Hz beat on the coinciding 4:5 pair) so you **hear** the roughness return and **watch** the field start to throb — toggle back and it locks. **Alive on a muted phone with zero permissions:** a seeded `mulberry32(0x9688)` auto-walker (never `Math.random`) steps fifths/thirds/septimals every ~2.5 s so the field breathes freeze→throb→freeze from mount, WebGL animating within ~1 s; first arrow/tap hands over. Audio (additive sine stacks, root drone + walked voice) through `createSafeMaster` @0.16 → limiter, gated behind the first gesture; the visual runs before any `AudioContext`. DEEP-mode winner (cycle 1087): ONE north star — **"consonance you can SEE"** — raced via 2 approaches, off EVERY jury ban (his-piano input · WebGPU-curl-noise-particle-field output · warm-amber vibe · cosmic-indigo vibe · **pentatonic tuning** — this is just intonation, cashing JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #5 "ban pentatonic → force microtonal/just-intonation"). ### [9624-counterpoint](/dream/9624-counterpoint) · **Play a phrase and the machine ANSWERS it in real counterpoint — a canon against itself, the subject inverted underneath, thickening into a small living fugue-exposition you conduct just by playing** · clinical **ink-on-high-key manuscript** — pale ground, thin dark ink staves + noteheads, ONE restrained brand-violet accent on the entering voice (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-glow, NO particle-field) · **COUNTERPOINT — cycle 1085 DEEP winner; cycle 2 of the jury-named "conceptually richest build" `9080-mnemonic`, extending it per JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #6 ("extend, don't restart — ship the cycle 2 of a 4–5-criteria build").** Cycle 1 quoted ONE motif back transformed on a second staff — a single one-off echo. The load-bearing NEW subsystem is a **long-horizon theme memory** (`reinforceTheme()`, `THEME_HALF_LIFE = 120 s` — a horizon in *minutes*): recurring shapes are tracked by interval contour and their **strength** climbs on each return / decays when abandoned; strength drives **stretto** — `voiceCountForStrength` grows the texture **2→3→4** and entry spacing shrinks as a theme intensifies, so you watch the exposition assemble over minutes. ### [9640-latencyloom](/dream/9640-latencyloom) · **A shared room where several tabs/people weave one piece and the network latency BETWEEN them is the instrument — each player's note reaches the others late, so the room plays itself as a distributed canon you re-tune with a delay slider** · clinical high-key network diagram — paper ground, ink nodes/edges, pulses crossing edges = visible canon offsets, violet `--primary` for the local node (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO particle field) · **LATENCY LOOM — cycle 1086 WIDE winner; the lab's FIRST multi-user piece (grep-0 across 1000+ protos), cashing the jury's headline 0× lane (JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #3: "zero multi-user in 15 cycles").** Real serverless transport via `BroadcastChannel("dream-9640-latencyloom")` — every open tab is a live player; playing a note broadcasts `{id,pitch,distanceMs,triggerShared}` and every client **re-synthesizes locally** (Cornelljam pattern, zero audio streamed). BroadcastChannel is ~instant so inter-peer distance is *simulated* per player: a note's onset is scheduled delayed by the sender's distance and quantized UP to the next tick of a shared 110-BPM 8th-note grid (off `performance.timeOrigin+now()`, identical across tabs — the Global Metronome, Oda & Fiebrink NIME 2016), so different latencies become whole-tick **canon offsets** — musical, never mud. The **0–1200 ms distance slider re-tunes the canon live** (latency-as-instrument, NIME 2025). Tuning = **7-limit just-intonation** `[1/1,9/8,5/4,4/3,3/2,5/3,7/4,2/1]` over ~196 Hz (grep-0 non-pentatonic), one waveform+pan per lane. Visual = Canvas2D clinical high-key: each player a node, each note a pulse travelling sender→receivers whose transit time = that peer's latency (you SEE the offset), a ticking time-grid. Three seeded `mulberry32` synthetic peers auto-join on mount so a muted phone sees a living network with zero interaction; real tabs join alongside. `prefers-reduced-motion` swaps travelling dots for a soft edge tint. All sound through `createSafeMaster` @0.18. Degrades to synthetic-only + notice if `BroadcastChannel` is undefined. Refs: NIME 2025 latency-as-instrument · GloMe · Cornelljam. **status: demoable** · design notes in-folder.

### [9592-disintegration](/dream/9592-disintegration) · **A recording you can only ever hear FEWER times — a piece that permanently, irreversibly erases itself as it plays, until it decays to true silence and cannot be recovered without starting over** · stark monochrome — papery near-white/ash ground + accumulating low-contrast film-grain dust (NO warm-amber, NO cosmic-indigo, NO glow, NO particle-field) · **DISINTEGRATION — cycle 1084 WIDE winner; the lab's FIRST conceptual/critical piece (grep-0 across the whole history) and the jury's boldest, most-emphatic monoculture-break (JURY 2026-08-10 provocation #4: "the direction most likely to break the aesthetic monoculture, because it isn't about being pretty").** The loop is an array of scheduled note-events (grains) — a **just-intonation** drone chord (ratios 1/1, 5/4, 3/2, 15/8, 2/1 over a low D2 ~73 Hz, deliberately NOT pentatonic). A single `DecayState` is the "tape" and one function, `advancePass()`, mutates it — and it can only move the state toward decay: it **permanently kills a grain** (`alive → false`, high partials eroding first the way tape sheds its top end; never restored) and monotonically raises `erosion` (0→1), which lowers a global lowpass (~2100→130 Hz), drops gain toward zero, and widens the silence between events. There is **no code path that restores a killed grain or lowers erosion**. Over ~1–3 minutes the loop empties, the grain-dust thickens, and it fades to true silence (`done`); the SOLE recovery is **"Begin again"**, which allocates a fresh pristine state from zero — you cannot rewind, only start over. ### [8728-luthier](/dream/8728-luthier) · **mass-interaction physical modeling — WIRE YOUR OWN INSTRUMENT: the network you see vibrating IS the waveform you hear** · blueprint steel links warming to brass under strain on near-black (NO violet, NO graphite/amber machine-partner, NO drone) · **THE LUTHIER — a blank "workbench" where there is no separate synthesizer. You DROP point masses, WIRE spring+damper links between them, GROUND anchors, mark a LISTENER node, then PLUCK — and the whole object rings. ### [7800-strikefield](/dream/7800-strikefield) · physical-modeling / organic / **HEAR *WHERE* A SOUND IS STRUCK — a resonant plate whose timbre changes with the strike position, made audible AND visible as its Chladni figure reshapes.** A resonant rectangular plate rendered as a live **Chladni standing-wave field** (Canvas2D) and voiced by **acoustic-transfer modal synthesis** (Web Audio). A `5×4=20`-mode resonator bank (mode grid `f(m,n)∝√((m/Lx)²+(n/Ly)²)`); **the key mechanic** — a strike at contact point `(sx,sy)` excites each mode weighted by its mode-shape amplitude there, `|sin(mπsx)·sin(nπsy)|`, so striking a **node** keeps that mode silent and an **antinode** makes it ring: position → timbre, the coupling NeuroSonic (2026) *learns* as a neural field, computed here in closed form. ### [6808-spectrascale](/dream/6808-spectrascale) · adult / scale-from-timbre / **THE SCALE ITSELF IS MADE OF THE TIMBRE — a keyboard organ whose entire set of playable pitches is GROWN from the instrument's spectrum in real time. Sethares' deepest thesis, made playable: every timbre has its own consonant scale. Sweep a second copy of the current spectrum across an octave, sum the sensory dissonance at every interval, and the local MINIMA of that dissonance curve ARE the consonant scale steps for that timbre. Reshape the sound with the drawbars (or the octave-stretch / inharmonicity sliders) and the whole curve re-flows and the scale re-lays-out live — a pure harmonic tone grows just intonation (valleys land on 5/4, 4/3, 3/2), while a stretched or metallic/inharmonic tone grows a genuinely alien, non-12-TET scale you can then play. Tuning follows timbre, at the scope of the whole scale.** · **INPUT = computer keyboard + drawbar/stretch/inharmonicity sliders** (number/letter row `1 2 3 … 0 q w e r …` plays the current derived degrees in order, `e.repeat`-guarded; ≥44px on-screen degree buttons for touch; 8 drawbar partial-amplitude sliders + an octave-stretch `S` + an inharmonicity `B` + a preset row Harmonic/Stretched/Metallic/Odd-only reshape the timbre → the curve and scale **re-derive live**) — a *played* instrument, never self-playing. A seeded (`mulberry32(0x6808)`) auto-demo morphs the timbre harmonic⇄stretched⇄metallic⇄odd on load (silent until the Start gesture) so the curve re-flows and the scale re-lays-out on a silent 06:30 phone glance with **zero permission**; yields instantly to real input. · **OUTPUT = pure DOM + CSS, ZERO GPU** — the dissonance curve is ~200 absolutely-positioned `<div>` bars (height = dissonance at that interval); valleys are highlighted violet and labeled with cents + nearest low-complexity just ratio; a thin grid marks the 12-TET semitones so the departure from equal temperament is visible; all motion is CSS `transform`/`transition`. **No `<canvas>` / `<svg>` / WebGL / WebGPU / three.js** — a dissonance-curve data-plot is a fresh OUTPUT metaphor in the lab (most differentiated from `6728`'s lattice-map and `6744`'s phase-space dots), pure-DOM →3× (off the last-10 Canvas2D-3× / SVG-3× near-guards); the lab's **NINTH straight non-GPU cycle**. · **TECHNIQUE = Sethares dissonance-curve scale construction / adaptive tuning from timbre** (0× shipped in the lab): `computeSpectrum` builds the partials from 8 drawbars + octave-stretch + inharmonicity (partial n at ratio `n^log₂(S)·√(1+B·n²)`); `dissmeasure(freqs,amps)` is the standard Plomp–Levelt/Sethares roughness (Dstar=0.24, s1=0.0207, s2=18.96, C1=5, C2=−5, A1=−3.51, A2=−5.75); `computeScale` sweeps interval α∈[1,2] in 200 steps evaluating `dissmeasure` of the spectrum against an α-shifted copy; `findValleys` = prominence-gated local minima → the playable degrees. Additive audio voice built from the SAME partials, so what you hear IS what the curve is computed from (10-voice oldest-steal, `DynamicsCompressor` limiter, master 0.18). **Verified minima:** harmonic → 388/496/705/886¢ (≈5/4, 4/3, 3/2, 5/3 — just intonation); stretched → 346/422/634/767¢ (no valley near 702); metallic & odd-only give entirely different non-12-TET sets. · **VIBE = microtonal / music-theory / spectral** (off the transcendent-cosmic ban — it's a spectral-tuning microscope, not a violet world that plays itself; off the tactile-instrument near-guard). ### [5720-lattice](/dream/5720-lattice) · adult / analytical-harmonic / **SEE THE SHAPE OF A CHORD — play, and every note lights a point in a rotating 3D crystal of pitch-space; a triad snaps into a small compact triangle, a dissonance spreads into a stretched polygon, and a bright marker glides through the crystal naming the key you're in** · **Web-MIDI (primary) / mic-pitch / seeded self-playing demo → Elaine Chew's SPIRAL ARRAY harmonic-geometry engine + center-of-effect tonal analysis → a three.js glowing helix crystal (lit nodes + fading voice-leading path + chord polygons + the drifting center-of-effect marker) + a clean Web Audio synth** · status: `demoable`. A real-time **tonal microscope** built on **Elaine Chew's Spiral Array** — the freshest *subject* the lab has taken on (harmonic geometry as a navigable crystal; grep shows the flat Tonnetz used before but not Chew's helical Spiral Array + its center-of-effect device). It cashes the fresh **jury (2026-08-02)**'s most-named starved input head-on: *"MIDI/MPE shipped exactly once (`4616-pressing`) and it was a standout … Build a MIDI-primary piece."* — this is Web-MIDI-primary, and directly **live-performance-fit for a pianist** (Karel care #3: plug in a keyboard and watch your harmony become geometry). **THE GEOMETRY (the substance, `spiral.ts`, from scratch):** pitches are wound along the *line of fifths* into a helix — node `k` at `x=R·sin(kπ/2), y=k·h, z=R·cos(kπ/2)` (R≈1, h≈0.4) so consecutive `k` are a perfect fifth apart and four steps complete one turn. The winding makes harmony *visible*: a **major triad** (root, fifth, major-third = `k, k+1, k+4`) puts its third one full turn directly above the root → a small compact triangle; a **minor triad** (`k, k+1, k−3`) is equally compact; a **dissonant cluster** spreads its vertices into a stretched polygon. Each pitch class is a violet-ramp glowing sphere labelled with its note name; a sounded note is drawn at the helix representation **nearest the current center of effect** (Chew's nearest-spelling resolution, keeping voice-leading local). **THE CENTER OF EFFECT (`page.tsx`):** the bright drifting marker is Chew's actual tonal-analysis device — the **exponentially-weighted centroid** (τ≈1.1 s) of the pitches sounding over the last ~2 s; where it settles estimates the tonal region/key, shown live as a readout, and it glides through the crystal as you play. **THE PAYOFF:** nodes bloom (scale + emissive + additive halo) on note-on; a fading additive polyline traces voice-leading; a translucent centroid-fan polygon draws whenever ≥3 notes sound — so a ii–V (spread Dm7/G7 four-note shapes) audibly-and-visibly **resolves** to a compact C-major triangle. **WHAT YOU SEE (silent-legible):** the crystal auto-rotates (~6°/s, no strobe) from page-load; on Start the seeded `mulberry32(0x5720)` **ii–V–I-in-C demo** auto-plays; and a readout panel narrates input mode, center-of-effect region, sounding notes, and the named chord shape — so a 06:30 phone review reads the whole concept with zero sound and zero interaction. **INPUT modes degrade:** Web MIDI (`requestMIDIAccess()` behind Start; hidden if absent) → **mic pitch** (normalized-autocorrelation → nearest MIDI note; `text-destructive` notice on denial) → **always-on seeded demo**. ### [5576-reflections](/dream/5576-reflections) · adult / spatial-installation / **WALK INTO A ROOM AND HEAR ITS SHAPE — every wall throws the sound back at you, and as you move through the space the echoes re-mirror and sweep around your head; the room's acoustics re-render around you, drawn live as folded reflection rays on an architectural plan** · **keyboard/click navigation + device-orientation head-turn → a from-scratch geometric IMAGE-SOURCE-METHOD acoustics engine → an SVG top-down plan (folded reflection paths + mirror-image ghosts) + binaural HRTF Web Audio** · status: `demoable`. The lab's **first moving-listener geometric room-acoustics** piece — and the direct answer to the **fresh jury (2026-08-02)**'s single most-repeated standing ask: *"Extend `5048-narthex` into the actual room … you have a working HRTF-spatial spine now — either put it in a real shared/embodied room this week or admit the installation lane is dead."* `5048-narthex` gave the lab an HRTF choir sphere with a **static** procedural convolution IR; its own README named the exact deepening — *"make the room's acoustics re-render as you move: replace the fixed reverb with a moving-listener early-reflection model, a bank of image-source taps recomputed as you cross the room."* This builds it. **THE TECHNIQUE (the substance, `acoustics.ts`, from scratch, no audio libraries):** a specular reflection off a flat wall is *exactly* a straight path from the source's **mirror image** across that wall — so for a shoebox room (8×5 m) you mirror each source across the 4 walls (first order), then again (second order) → a bounded **17 image sources per voice** (1 direct + 4 + 12); each image = one **audio tap** with **delay** = path/343 (`DelayNode`), **gain** = reflectionCoeff^order / max(1,path) (1/r spreading + per-bounce wall absorption 0.72), an **air-absorption low-pass** whose cutoff falls with path length, and **HRTF spatialization** through its own `PannerNode` (`panningModel:"HRTF"`) positioned *in the direction of the image source relative to the head* — so a reflection genuinely arrives from the wall that threw it. **THE PAYOFF:** as the listener walks/turns, `RoomAudio.update()` recomputes every distance/delay/gain/cutoff/panner-position and re-ramps them with `setTargetAtTime` (no zipper) — **the acoustics re-render around you.** 3 just-intoned voice-pads (major triad 1/1·5/4·3/2 over A2, detuned saws breathing on slow LFOs) keep the room ringing; everything sums through a `DynamicsCompressor` limiter, master ≤0.2. **WHAT YOU SEE (SVG/DOM only):** a top-down architectural **plan** — room walls (violet hairlines), the **folded reflection path** to each source (bolder/more opaque = louder tap), dashed **ghost lines** out to the first-order **mirror images beyond the walls** (with dim image-source markers — the whole method self-explanatory at a glance), breathing sources, and the **listener head-marker** with its facing triangle; a mono readout (room size · listener xy · active tap count · dominant reflection delay in ms). The full concept is legible from the SVG **in silence**. **INPUT:** WASD/arrows walk (relative to facing) + **click-a-point to walk there** (click-to-move target, NOT a drag) + **`DeviceOrientationEvent`** head-turn (iOS `requestPermission()` behind Start) / Q/E on desktop; a `mulberry32(0x5576)` **seeded auto-tour** walks the listener on a slow loop so it self-demos hands-free. **DEGRADES:** no headphones/audio → the SVG plan + auto-tour tell the whole story; orientation denied → keyboard nav still works + a `text-destructive` note; autoplay-safe (AudioContext only on Start); clean teardown. No strobe (slow luminance only), no camera, no api-route, no secrets. **INPUT = keyboard/click navigation + device-orientation head-turn (off the jury-banned pointer/touch-DRAG-on-a-field — this is spatial navigation, not a drag gesture; Also cashes Karel's live-performance-fitness care (#3). **THE ALGORITHM (the substance, `follow.ts`, from scratch, no deps, legible top-to-bottom):** a reference score (*Ode to Joy* theme, two 16-beat C-major phrases, `{pitchMidi,beatStart,beatDur}`) the follower knows → a dependency-free **autocorrelation pitch detector** (McLeod-style peak-pick + parabolic refine) + a stable-pitch onset gate over the mic `AnalyserNode` → the **`FollowerEngine`: an online-DTW / cost-grid forward tracker** holding a belief over score positions as an accumulated cost array, relaxed once per onset `cost'[j] = emission(pitch,j) + min_i(cost[i] + transition(i,j))`, where **emission** rewards an exact pitch (0), forgives an octave (0.35, common in autocorrelation) & a neighbour fumble (≤2 st → 0.85) & penalizes-but-**never-blocks** a far miss (so a wrong note costs a little and the tracker HOLDS its place instead of derailing), and **transition** prefers advance-one (0), tolerates stay-put (0.55, trill/held/repeat), and permits forward **skips** & backward **repeats** at distance-growing cost (tuned so an exact backward match beats a forward fumble but a clean forward exact still always wins); renormalized each step so repeats stay reachable, cold-start anchored by a soft position prior so two identical opening notes don't run the frontier ahead. **Confidence** = best-vs-second-best cost gap; **belief** = `softmax(−cost)` surfaced as the heat-glow on each score note (watch the distribution concentrate + spread); **live tempo** = score-beats ÷ real-seconds over recent *confident* advances, EMA-smoothed 40–300 BPM, which the **accompanist** (warm triangle/sine pad chords + soft bass pulse → `DynamicsCompressor`, master ≤0.2, gesture-gated) locks to so it audibly accelerates, ritards, and **waits**. Every onset is classified into a legible on-screen event — `advance` · `skip detected +n` · `wrong note ignored` · `repeat matched −n`. **HEADLESS-VERIFIED:** a `mulberry32(0x5528)` **synthetic performer** "plays" the score with deliberate rubato + one wrong note + one skip-ahead + one repeated phrase, and a test harness confirmed the engine resolves all four hard cases IN ORDER (`skip detected +3` → `wrong note ignored (C♯4≠D4)` → `repeat matched −3`) with **zero** ground-truth position drift >1 note through the rubato — so on load the piece **self-demos hands-free** and a silent 06:30 review sees the whole tracking legibly with zero sound. **DEGRADES:** no mic/headless → the synthetic performer drives everything (silent until *Begin*); mic denied → `text-destructive` notice + demo keeps running; autoplay-safe (no `AudioContext` until first gesture); clean teardown of rAF/context/mic. ### [5480-development](/dream/5480-development) · adult / compositional-architectural / **A PIECE THAT COMPOSES ITSELF FORWARD AND REMEMBERS — one germ motif stated, then grown across a whole arc (inverted, reversed, augmented, fragmented, sequenced, modulated) with real memory, so the end is a provable transformation of the beginning, never a loop** · **self-playing → a symbolic motivic-transformation engine → a self-writing Canvas2D piano-roll + live derivation trace** · status: `demoable`. The lab's **first symbolic self-developing long-form composer** — a genuinely new VERB on music (compose & develop, not paint/understand/duet/sonify) and the "long-form generative with state/memory/evolution" menu lane the lab is thin on. Cashes the fresh **jury (2026-08-02)** provocations *"kill the field-sim reflex — build something discrete/symbolic/agentic, interaction logic not PDE integration"* + *"if you touch the piano, change the verb."* **THE ENGINE:** (1) **`engine.ts`** — a germ = an array of `{degree, duration}` over an Aeolian scale; the classical & dodecaphonic operators as pure functions (**Prime · Inversion** [intervals mirrored around an axis] **· Retrograde · Retrograde-Inversion · Transpose · Augment/Diminish** [durations scaled] **· Fragment · Sequence · Modulate**), each with an audible identity (augmentation broadens, the climax stabs diminished fragments an octave up, modulation moves the key). A **`Conductor` state machine** walks a narrative arc — **exposition → development → climax → recapitulation → coda** — then rolls up a fourth into a new movement so it never stops; each phase draws operators from its own palette applied to **remembered** phrases. (2) **memory** — every emitted phrase is stored with its `parents` + a `lineage` of op-tags (`seed → I → aug → …`); recapitulation literally quotes-and-transforms earlier memory, and the live UI shows the current lineage as a **derivation trace**, making late material a *provable descendant* of the germ. (3) **`audio.ts`** — warm pluck lead + triangle/sine bass + detuned-saw pad through a feedback delay + compressor, a 25 ms look-ahead scheduler scheduling ~200 ms ahead of `AudioContext.currentTime`. ### [5432-tremorsong](/dream/5432-tremorsong) · adult / documentary-geophysical / **HEAR THE LAST 24 HOURS OF THE LIVING EARTH — every earthquake on the planet as a note, sequenced by when it happened, pitched by its depth, struck by its magnitude — a real-time seismic score you play back and watch ripple across a world map** · **live external data (USGS `all_day.geojson`, CORS, no-auth) → a from-scratch parameter-mapping sonification engine → a Canvas2D equirectangular world map + timeline** · status: `demoable`. The lab's **first piece about the physical world / a live external feed** — *music about something other than music*, the "real-world data sonification" menu category the **fresh jury (2026-08-02)** names as thin and nobody occupied. Cashes the jury's loudest demand — **RANGE** — hardest: after a window that was 9-of-15 visionary-field-sims, this is the Earth itself as the instrument. **THE PIPELINE:** (1) **`data.ts`** client-`fetch`es the public USGS feed, parses each GeoJSON feature → `{mag,time,place,lon,lat,depth}`, sorts by time; on any failure/offline/headless it falls to a baked ~42-quake realistic 24h snapshot (mag 1.1–6.8, depth 5–612 km, real tectonic coords) — a badge reads **live · USGS** or **sample data**. ### [5000-anneal](/dream/5000-anneal) · adult / visionary-INTENSE / **A SOLID THAT MELTS AS YOU PLAY IT — "press a crystal until it yields and slumps into liquid, and hear the exact moment the solid becomes a fluid"** · **pointer press/drag + phone tilt → WebGL2 additive point/line glow (Canvas2D fallback) + a struck modal-bell bank whose timbre IS the material's stiffness** · The lab's **first physics-based sonification** — the direct build of RESEARCH §984's *BioSonix* dive (arXiv:2508.14688, 2026): rather than mapping a scalar to pitch, it runs a physical deformation sim and lets the sim's internal **stress excite a resonant body whose modal timbre encodes the material's current stiffness**, so the sound is not a readout of the melt — it *is* the material being deformed. A ~38×38 **mass-spring/soft-body lattice** (structural + shear springs, Verlet, 2 substeps/frame, `performance.now()` timing) carries a per-node `melt` scalar in [0,1]; when a spring's relative strain crosses a yield threshold it *heats* its two nodes toward melting, melting collapses that spring's effective stiffness (`kEff→0`) so the ordered grid visibly **slumps into liquid slush**, and when force is released `melt` decays and the grid **anneals** back toward crystal. Per-node **strain energy** (`½·k·Δ²`) is exported every frame as the composer. **AUDIO (the physics-based-sonification payload):** the whole screen is ONE struck crystal bell whose 6 modes map to 6 lattice regions (2×3); per-region strain-energy RATE is an impact feeding a strike envelope into that mode's excitation (`noise → excitation gain → bandpass resonator → low-pass smear → gain → master → DynamicsCompressor limiter`), and **`melt` reshapes the timbre continuously along three axes at once** — a hard crystal rings **bright, high-Q, inharmonic** (bell partials `0.5,1,1.2,1.5,2,2.667 × 196 Hz`); as a region melts its mode **detunes downward, its Q collapses, and the low-pass closes**, smearing it into a soft watery wash with a slow deterministic liquid shimmer. So a hard region and a molten region sound categorically different, and the crossing is audible — not a played note-grid, a continuous excitation model. **RENDER:** WebGL2 additive point+line glow, colour encoding state (cool violet crystal on the ordered grid → warm liquid-ember where melted, strain adds bloom); Canvas2D fallback if WebGL2 is missing. Self-demos silently: a seeded (`mulberry32(0x5000)`, never `Math.random`) 12 s force-sweep presses → melts → anneals on loop so a silent 06:30 phone sees the whole arc hands-free, audio joins on **Start** (autoplay-gated); real pointer or iOS-`requestPermission`-gated tilt hands control over. Graceful: no WebGL2 → Canvas2D lattice; no tilt → pointer-only; `prefers-reduced-motion` → gentler slump, less jitter, fewer points. ### [4904-criticality](/dream/4904-criticality) · adult / visionary-INTENSE / **YOUR VOICE TIPS A FIELD PAST CRITICALITY AND THE CROSSING IS EGO-DISSOLUTION — "long-range order shatters into scale-free entropy, and the boundary between you and everything dissolves"** · **mic (real Web-Audio `AnalyserNode` — RMS loudness + an 80–350 Hz low-band "alpha-analogue" proxy) → WebGL2 fullscreen fragment-shader field (Canvas2D fallback) + a consonant additive drone that decoheres in lockstep** · Renders the *mechanism* of a visionary peak, not its content. A 2D field sits **poised just below its critical point** (`P_CRIT = 0.62`): below criticality it shows a bright coherent "self" — a symmetric radial standing-wave mandala with visible long-range order, localized against a dark surround (the boundary between you and everything). Your **sustained voice is the control parameter** `pressure`: it pushes the field **past the critical point**, where a **correlation-length bloom diverges** (critical opalescence — all-scale fluctuations, seen as a swell + heard as a surge) and the **order parameter collapses** (`order = ((Pc−p)/Pc)^0.55` → 0) so long-range order **shatters into 1/f scale-free entropic turbulence** that fills the whole frame — no center, no boundary, a boundless glowing medium. **That crossing is the ego-dissolution.** Fall silent and (asymmetric attack ~0.85 s / release ~2.6 s) the self slowly re-coheres. The consonant additive drone (8 harmonic partials of 110 Hz) dissolves in lockstep: partials detune (cents ∝ entropy) + drift inharmonic, a broadband noise floor rises (lowpass opens ~240 Hz→6 kHz), reverb widens toward a boundary-less space, a swell marks the critical bloom — so order→entropy is heard as well as seen, through a limiter. **SAFETY (photosensitive epilepsy) — built in:** NO strobe by default; motion is slow luminance *drift* (phase advances at a clamped ~0.6 rad/s base, +≤1.4 rad/s on opt-in *Intensify*, so per-pixel luminance oscillates far under the ~3 Hz danger band); an always-visible *Calm / Stop* freezes all motion + silences the drone the same frame; `prefers-reduced-motion` damps to 0.4×; order/entropy change on the seconds-long *voice* timescale so brightness drifts, never flickers. Degrades: mic denied → deterministic `mulberry32(0x4904)` seeded auto-demo scripts a full voice envelope (rest→build→cross→boundless dissolution→release→re-cohere, loop ~17 s), the field self-paints a coherent self from frame 1 (audio on first tap), `text-destructive` notice explains the fallback; no WebGL2 → Canvas2D order→entropy field; no Web Audio → field still runs with a no-sound notice. ### [4440-vow](/dream/4440-vow) · adult / **SCARCITY-AS-INSTRUMENT — "every strike is spent forever"** · **deliberate touch/pointer strikes → three.js (no Canvas2D, no shader field)** · **twelve struck resonant "vows" hang in a dark constellation, but the whole instrument holds a FINITE reserve of 108 strikes — EVER — persisted across every visit; each tap spends one permanently, the struck node dims and never fully returns, the field cools as the count falls, and at zero it goes silent forever. Each vow is REAL modal/banded struck-resonator synthesis (Julius O. Smith): a bank of inharmonic modes, each an oscillator whose decay time-constant is **τ = Q/(π·f)** so bright high modes damp fastest (the frequency-dependent damping of struck metal/glass falls out of the physics) — four hand-voiced archetypes (bell / glass / bar / bowl) across the 12 nodes = a genuine scale of timbres, never a sample or sine beep; seeded `mulberry32(0x4440)` per-strike jitter so no two strikes are identical; limiter on the bus. three.js constellation of icosahedra + additive halos + UnrealBloom, neighbour-coupling ripple on strike, per-node permanent wear, a farewell ~3× stretched decay on the last strike then fade to near-black. ### [3248-crowd](/dream/3248-crowd) · adult / conceptual-critical · working-memory / retroactive-interference · **tap notes into a ~5-slot memory; each new note steals activation from the ones already held — you steer what survives** / **Canvas2D activation ring + interference arrows + gravestones + capacity meter, 2-osc voices whose loudness/brightness = how well the note is "held in mind"** · cycle 929 · DEEP-winner (2026-07-29) · demoable · `vibe: conceptual / critical / poignant — memory as a zero-sum attention economy; "adding a note is choosing what to lose"`. **The one question:** what if memory had a hard capacity — so every new note you played pushed an older one toward being forgotten? **The model (`memory.ts`, pure functions the UI + headless check both drive):** a budget of ~5 active notes, each with an **activation** in [0,1]; encoding a NEW note injects its own activation and **subtracts** from the held notes via **retroactive interference** that is **similarity-weighted** (more stolen from notes close in pitch/time), **recency-weighted** (recent traces more vulnerable), and **vulnerability-weighted** (`VULN_GAMMA 2.2` — already-weak traces bleed fastest, winner-take-all), all scaled by memory **load** (`Σact/BUDGET`) so a near-empty memory doesn't compete and a full one competes hard → the pool is near-conserved and bounded near capacity. Below `EVICT_THRESHOLD 0.2` a note is **forgotten** — drops out of the loop, goes silent, crumbles to a dim **gravestone**. **Rehearsal** re-injects a held note toward 1.0 (fresh single-exposure tops out at `0.92`, so a rehearsed favourite is *strictly* strongest) — but it too steals from the others, so you *feel* the trade-off of defending one. Continuous pitch on the ring (A2–A5, **never scale-snapped**). AudioContext lookahead scheduler (25 ms/120 ms, absolute `ctx.currentTime`), 110 BPM; activation → loudness + lowpass brightness + presence; 20:1 limiter → 0.15 master. Opens self-demoing (seeded `mulberry32` auto-taps 8 notes into capacity-5 then rehearses 2 favourites); Start arms audio. **Refs:** **Miller "7±2" (1956)** + **Cowan ≈4 (2001)** + **McGeoch retroactive interference (1932)** + RESEARCH §929 (arXiv:2606.15088 — forgetting is heterogeneous; here driven by *competition*, not neglect). Headless-proven a **property of the model, not the seed**: across seeds 99/42/7/1337/2024 survivors settle to 4–5 (≤ budget), ≥3 evicted to activation 0, and the 2 rehearsed notes are always strictly highest (1.00). DEEP cycle 929 raced it against two banked ⭐⭐ HIGH siblings on the same north star (`3232-fade` Ebbinghaus+SM-2 forgetting-curve w/ AudioWorklet crush, `3256-recall` reconsolidation lossy-recall — IDEAS §929); both siblings' ideas folded into its README as next-cycle deepening.

### [3200-downbeat](/dream/3200-downbeat) · adult / instrument-craft · performance · musical-stakes · **you CONDUCT a small ensemble and your beat IS the performance — tap the pulse (space bar / phone tilt) and a two-bar arrangement follows *you*: hold clear even time and the players lock into a tight groove, rush and they crowd behind you, drag and they run ahead** / a conducting instrument built on a **phase-locked-loop tempo tracker + AudioContext lookahead scheduler** — the most complete reading of jury-2026-07-27 #3 (*dial → **decision***, "extend the pieces with real musical stakes") and it refills the **SVG** output register jury #2 flagged as cratered to 1×. **The concept:** the vocal-duet extension of `2920-follow` the jury keeps naming was already built (`3120-continuator`, cycle 923); the *un-built* seam in the same "human owns a musical decision" family is **ensemble timing you conduct** — a tempo that is yours to hold, where holding it badly is audible. **The technique (`pll.ts` + `scheduler.ts` + `synth.ts`):** each beat you give updates a running tempo estimate — the **period** (seconds/beat) follows your inter-tap interval at a low gain and the beat **phase** (a continuous grid, `gridTimeOf(index)`) is nudged toward where your tap actually landed; the gentle gains make the grid **smooth**, so a sudden rush/drag makes the ensemble's grid *lag your hand* — that lag is the instrument. The ensemble is never a fixed metronome: a **lookahead scheduler** (~150 ms ahead, every rAF) finds each note of a two-bar A-minor phrase (walking bass · chord stabs · FM melody) whose position falls on the *current conducted grid* and calls `osc.start(when)` at a precise `AudioContext.currentTime` offset — steady conducting → a tight even onset grid; rushing → the notes flam against your tick. A short bandpass "tick" on each conductor beat makes the pulse audible against the downbeat. **Verified headless** (simulated steady vs rushed tap streams through the real `pll.ts`+`scheduler.ts`, measuring conductor-vs-ensemble phase gap + flam): **STEADY mean |gap| 2.7 ms / flam 2.6 ms (locked); RUSH gap 149 ms / flam 112 ms; DRAG gap 128 ms / flam 69 ms** — near-zero error when steady, a large systematic lag when rushing/dragging, so the "you can get it wrong" stakes provably manifest in the *timing*, decisive for a silent 06:30 review. **The stakes, as geometry (`wheel.tsx`, SVG):** a **phase-wheel** carries the ensemble's beat marker (filled) and your beat marker (hollow); the arc between them is your timing error in ms, colouring from violet toward magenta as it opens (meet = locked, split = fighting the groove); three scrolling **note-lanes** below show upcoming scheduled notes landing on the grid at the "now" line with your taps marked above. SVG only — no canvas, no WebGL. **Pitch policy (clears the JI-net ban by construction):** the arrangement's pitches (including the pentatonic melody) are a *fixed composed line* — there is **no continuous-pitch input to quantize**; the human's input is **time** (beat taps), so the protected continuous-pitch stakes are untouched, exactly as `3144`/`3192` handled it. **Input = conducting-beat via keyboard-Space + tilt** (deliberately OFF the diversity-banned touch/pointer register): Space keydown = one beat (the featured, fully-working desktop input for the morning review); on a phone `DeviceOrientationEvent` beta-axis down-strokes = beats (iOS `requestPermission` behind a button; unavailable/denied → keyboard, silently). **Headless-safe solo demo:** on load a seeded **`mulberry32(0x3200)` auto-conductor** holds steady ~9 s so the groove locks, then deliberately **rushes toward ~143 bpm** and **drags toward ~71 bpm** so the lock→slip behaviour is audible + visible with no human (LIVE/DEMO via "Take the baton" / "Demo"; "Tap beat" on-screen fallback). ### [3192-bow](/dream/3192-bow) · adult / instrument-craft · physical-modeling · musical-stakes · **the screen teaches you to BOW a string — bow speed and pressure are a 2-D gesture, and too little force whispers, too much force screeches, only the right zone sings; you play *on* the Schelleng playability wedge and hear the instant you fall out** / a bowed-string **stick–slip friction** instrument — the most literal reading of *a musical decision you can get wrong* (jury-2026-07-27 #3, dial→**decision**), and the register jury #2 named (get off the fragment shader — SVG had cratered to 1×). **The concept:** real bowing forgives nothing because the string's physics don't; this piece models that physics and turns its playable zone into the interface. **The friction model (the sound):** a **digital-waveguide** bowed string — two fractional delay lines are the string either side of the bow (their length sets pitch) with a low-pass bridge-reflection loss — driven at the bow point by a **nonlinear friction junction** (McIntyre, Woodhouse & Schumacher, 1983): each sample forms the *relative velocity* between bow and string and a friction curve returns a coupling coefficient — near-zero rel-velocity = **stick** (bow drags the string), large = **slip** (bow skates free); the stick↔slip alternation *is* Helmholtz motion, *is* the tone. Your gesture reaches it as two knobs — **bow speed → bow velocity**, **bow force → the friction-curve slope** (capture width): a large slope (light bow) = narrow capture, the string can't lock → a thin surface whistle; a small slope (heavy bow) = wide capture, the string over-sticks and the release goes irregular → a raucous crunch; between them it sings. Timbre change is the friction nonlinearity, **not** a filter sweep. Two force-dependent terms sharpen the extremes so all three regimes are unmistakable — **bridge damping falls as force rises** (a light bow can't overcome the loss → stays quiet; the minimum-bow-force effect) and a **slip-breakdown term above force≈0.7** adds an energy-growing perturbation (the multi-slipping of an over-pressed string), *exactly zero inside the singing band*. **Verified headless** (RMS + autocorrelation on the steady tail): singing autocorrelation ≈ **1.0** (locked/periodic), raucous ≈ **0.43** (genuinely aperiodic, not merely louder) — the stakes provably manifest in the *sound*, which is why this one shipped over its siblings for a silent review. **The Schelleng diagram (the stakes, as geometry):** Schelleng (1973) — the clean-tone region is a **wedge** in the bow-force/motion plane, `F_min ∝ v/β²` (min force **rises** with speed) and `F_max ∝ 1/(βv)` (max force **falls** with speed), so the wedge **narrows and pinches shut** as you bow faster — fast bowing is unforgiving. The diagram **is** the bow strip: drag horizontally = speed, vertically = force; a live crosshair sits where your gesture is, colored by regime (surface / **singing** / raucous), and the same (speed,force) numbers drive both the diagram and the synth so sight and sound agree. A second SVG panel animates the **traveling Helmholtz corner** (a ~140-point polyline that ramps up as the string captures, ripples thin in surface, jitters in raucous). Pitch is the discrete choice (G3/D4/A4/E5 via buttons / ←→ / 1–4 — the instrument's tuning); the **continuous, expressive input is the bow gesture, snapped to nothing** (clears the JI-net ban by construction). **Headless-safe solo demo:** on load a seeded **`mulberry32(0x3192)` auto-bow** sweeps too-light → into the wedge → too-hard, demonstrating all three regimes hands-free (**● auto** badge; visuals-only until you click, per autoplay policy — "Play the auto-demo with sound" or "Pick up the bow" / first pointer-down flips to **live**). **Audio path:** an **AudioWorklet** loaded from a **Blob URL** (no `public/` file needed under the dream-folder scope) runs the sample-rate friction loop; if `addModule` fails it falls back to a **ScriptProcessorNode** running the identical model (status line says which). **Safe by construction:** master gain 0.12 (≤0.15) → `DynamicsCompressor` limiter, clamped injection + DC blocker — a raucous bow can't blast or blow up. Clean teardown (rAF cancel · worklet/graph disconnect · Blob URL revoke · `AudioContext` close · listeners removed). **Named refs:** **McIntyre, Woodhouse & Schumacher, "On the oscillations of musical instruments," _JASA_ 74(5), 1983** (the friction bowed-string model) · **Schelleng, "The bowed string and the player," _JASA_ 53(1), 1973** (the playability wedge). **Subsystems (≥3):** pointer 2-D bow-gesture input + friction-waveguide DSP (`string.ts` / `worklet-source.ts`) + Schelleng envelope math & regime classifier (`schelleng.ts`) + dual-SVG viz (wedge + Helmholtz string) = 4. **Ambition — 3/5:** #1 (first bowed-friction / stick-slip waveguide *shipped* in the lab — distinct from `2952-tabla`'s *struck* 2-D waveguide mesh: this is a *bowed* 1-D friction junction) · #2 (≥3 subsystems = 4) · #3 (MWS 1983 + Schelleng 1973). **diversity:** last-10 ≈ [2992,3008,3040,3048,3056,3080,3120,3136,3144]; audit `banned` = [jury-2026-07-27: **fresh altered-states/psych-phenomenology** (8× moratorium) · **WebGL2 fragment-shader default output** (8×) · **shared visionary kit wired to one input scalar** · **re-adding the JI/pentatonic input net**]; `picked (fan)` = every candidate **instrument-with-stakes** (jury #3) on a **different input × output × technique** — this winner: **pointer bow-gesture** input (a *force/position* gesture, not the over-used slider-drag or voice) · **SVG** output (directly refilling the register jury #2 flagged as cratered to 1×; off the banned shader) · **bowed-friction waveguide** technique (fresh, 0× shipped) · **instrument-craft** vibe (NOT altered-states) — clears every live ban. **mode:** WIDE (ledger 921 W · 922 D · 923 D · 924 W · 925 D → **926 WIDE**; and WIDE directly attacks the standing "too similar" mandate — three unrelated instruments in one fire). ONE posture — *three instruments where a human owns a musical decision that can be wrong* — across three attacks. **candidates:** 3192-bow(win — purest dial→**decision**, cashes jury #2's SVG gap, and the *only* candidate to prove its stakes headless via the autocorrelation regime test — decisive when the reviewer can't listen; canonical MWS/Schelleng refs; a real physical-modeling instrument is deeply on-brand for a "personal audio workspace for composers") · 3176-baton(banked ⭐⭐ HIGH, IDEAS §926 — **conduct a synthesized ensemble; rushing/dragging pulls the players off the beat with you**; ambition 4/5, research-anchored to §926's dive (arXiv:2604.27957 conducting-gestures + Max Mathews' Radio-Baton/Conductor Program) — the truest research→build chain and the freshest *surprise*; held only because its felt drag-the-ensemble loop is genuinely unverifiable headless where the bow proved its stakes) · 3184-marble(banked ⭐, IDEAS §926 — **tilt a marble down a switchback of tuned pegs to play a melody**; three.js + Wintergatan ref; held for the loosest stakes — a bad roll *stalls into a fragment* rather than sounding wrong — and unverifiable tilt feel). Both losers `rm -rf`'d after banking full IDEAS §926 briefs, before the authoritative winner-only build (never committed). **No API route → no `guard`** (pure `"use client"` Web Audio + SVG; zero new npm deps, no server route, no secrets, no side effects). **Validation:** normalizer = **0 rewrites** (on-brand: raw color confined to the SVG art — indigo/violet/red regime fills — semantic-token chrome, `min-h-[44px]`/`rounded-md bg-primary` primary + `border-border bg-background/60` secondary, `bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm`/`shadow-lg` modal, `font-mono text-xs` labels, `text-destructive` for the raucous failure, no `text-white`/`font-serif`/off-brand-hue chrome; helpers `make*`/`classify*`/`bow*`/`clamp*` — no non-hook `use*`); winner-folder `next lint --max-warnings 0` = clean; authoritative winner-only `next build --experimental-build-mode compile` = **EXIT 0**, `/dream/3192-bow` present in `app-path-routes-manifest.json` (count 1; losers absent from `src` and `.next`). (Full-route `npm run build` still overflows the container's hard **4096-fd** cap across ~880 routes during whole-app static-page-data collection — the standing infra condition every recent cycle, not code; Vercel has headroom and runs the full pipeline on deploy.) **NOT ear-verified** (headless — no speakers): the friction constants (bow-table slope range, loop damping, capture width) are physically shaped and the three regimes are correctly ordered + measured-distinct, but *where exactly each regime bites* along the gesture wants a real-ear tuning pass; the AudioWorklet/ScriptProcessor + pointer paths are type/lint-clean and code-reviewed but not runtime-exercised in a browser here (the Node DSP port that self-oscillates + the autocorrelation test are the silent-review stand-ins). `theme: bow a real friction string; stay in the playable wedge or it screeches · state: n/a · pole: n/a · vibe: instrument-craft, decision-stakes`. status: **demoable**

### [3144-latency](/dream/3144-latency) · adult / networked-performance · multi-user · musical-stakes · **two players turn the network round-trip between them into a deliberate musical CANON — measure the lag, snap it to a rhythmic subdivision, and the echo you *watch* land is the echo you *hear* land; tap ON the grid and note+echo interlock, tap OFF and the figure frays** / a two-player **latency-as-material** instrument (the lab's **second real multi-user piece** — first since `2912-ensemble`, cashing jury-2026-07-27 provocation #5). **The concept:** networked-music research spends its whole effort *fighting* delay toward the ~25 ms Ensemble Performance Threshold; NIME 2025 paper 69 flips it — *snap whatever latency exists onto a rhythmic grid so the round-trip becomes an intentional canon.* This is the browser reading of that: a Canvas2D **rhythm wheel** (one revolution = one bar of sixteenths at 90 BPM) where every note drops a mark at the playhead's angle, the measured round-trip latency is **snapped to the nearest subdivision** (`CANON_STEPS`, 1/32 … 1/4), and the angular **gap** between a note and its delayed echo is drawn as the canon interval — with a faint **pre-snap "ghost"** showing where the raw arrival landed vs. where the snap put it, so *you literally watch the latency being quantized onto the grid.* **The decision-stakes (jury #3, dial→decision):** the stakes are **rhythmic, not melodic** — a consonant D-pentatonic map means every subdivision is a good note, so only *timing* can be wrong; tap on a tick and note+echo interlock into a ringing figure, tap between ticks and the figure frays and the center "lock" glow dims. **Headless-safe solo demo:** default **loopback mode** — a `LoopbackPeer` echoes taps at an adjustable 40–320 ms round-trip + seeded jitter, and a seeded **`mulberry32`** auto-partner is already looping a phrase on the inner ring so a two-voice canon is audible/visible with zero interaction; drag the latency slider to re-drive the live raw-ms→snapped-subdivision readout. **The real two-phone path** (`RtcPeer`): opt-in **manual-SDP WebRTC** (create offer → send SDP text → paste answer back), **no signaling server, no api route, public STUN only, non-trickle single-paste ICE**, wrapped defensively so any failure/disconnect silently falls back to loopback. **Named refs:** **NIME 2025 paper 69 "Exploiting Latency in the Design of a Networked Music Performance"** (compose *with* delay, don't fight it to zero) · the **~25 ms Ensemble Performance Threshold** · **Chafe / CCRMA** latency-accepting networked ensembles (JackTrip). **Subsystems (≥3):** WebRTC data channel (`net.ts`, `RtcPeer` + `LoopbackPeer`) + latency measure-and-snap engine (`wheel.ts`, `snapLatency` with EMA-smoothed ping/pong RTT) + Web Audio pluck synth (`audio.ts`, triangle+sine partials, lowpass sweep, beat-synced feedback delay for canonic space, AudioContext-scheduled) + Canvas2D rhythm wheel (`wheel.ts`, `drawWheel`: grid, playhead, local/remote bands, canon-gap arcs, pre-snap ghosts, lock hub) = 4. **Ambition — 4/5:** #1 (first latency-as-material / first latency-snapped-canon; WebRTC multi-user was 1× prior) · #2 (≥3 subsystems = 4) · #3 (NIME 2025 p69 / EPT / Chafe-CCRMA) · #5 (RESEARCH §925, same-date). **diversity:** last-10 ≈ [2960,2992,3008,3040,3048,3056,3080,3120,3136]; audit `banned` = [jury-2026-07-27: **fresh altered-states/psych-phenomenology** (8× moratorium) · **WebGL2 fragment-shader as default output** (8×) · **shared visionary kit wired to one input scalar** · **re-adding the JI/pentatonic input net**]; `picked` = [**network** input (0× in last-10; not the over-used voice/touch) · **Canvas2D** output (off the banned WebGL shader) · **latency-as-canon** technique (fresh — 0×) · **networked-performance** vibe with **rhythmic decision-stakes** (NOT altered-states)] — clears every live ban. **Note on pentatonic:** the ban targets a *continuous-pitch input quantizer* (a snap-to-scale safety net that removes melodic stakes); 3144 has **no pitch input to quantize** — taps trigger fixed pads and the axis of play is deliberately *time*, so the fixed pentatonic is not the banned pattern. **mode:** DEEP (ledger 921 W · 922 D · 923 D · 924 W → **925 DEEP**; AGENT.md routes DEEP-on-X when a jury has a standing named "ship/extend X" — provocation #5's "build a second multi-user piece / ship banked `3144-latency`" + the ready ⭐⭐ HIGH banked brief MORNING §924 floated to Karel). ONE concept, three viz/interaction attacks. **candidates:** 3144-latency(win — the banked #1 HIGH item MORNING promised Karel; the pre-snap ghost makes the *concept* visible for a solo review; cleanest AudioContext-scheduled audio; canonical NIME reading) · 3160-relay(banked ⭐⭐ HIGH, IDEAS §925 — latency as *visible travel* across two shores; the strongest surprise/teaching, held as the natural companion / alternate render-mode) · 3168-lockstep(banked ⭐⭐ HIGH, IDEAS §925 — the *losable phase-lock game*, purest dial→decision, held because its audio is rAF-triggered ~16 ms-jitter not a lookahead scheduler — a real knock for a tight-rhythm piece; resurrect after moving to an AudioContext scheduler). Both losers `rm -rf`'d after banking full IDEAS §925 briefs, before the authoritative winner-only build (never committed). **No API route → no `guard`** (pure `"use client"` Web Audio + Canvas2D + browser-native WebRTC; zero new npm deps, no server route, no secrets, no side effects). **Validation:** normalizer = **0 rewrites** (on-brand semantic-token chrome, raw color confined to the Canvas art, `min-h-[44px]`/`rounded-md bg-primary` primary + `border-border bg-background/60` secondary buttons, `bg-background`/`shadow-lg` modals, `font-mono text-xs` labels, no `text-white`/`font-serif`/off-brand-hue chrome; helpers `draw*`/`make*`/`angle*`/`snap*`/`quantize*`/`pitch*` — no non-hook `use*`); winner-folder `next lint --max-warnings 0` clean; authoritative winner-only `next build --experimental-build-mode compile` = **EXIT 0**, `/dream/3144-latency` present in `app-path-routes-manifest.json` (count 1; losers absent from `src` and `.next`). ### [3136-tarab](/dream/3136-tarab) · adult / instrument · musical-stakes · **press ONE key and a whole body of sympathetic strings wakes behind it — the note you *decide* to play blooms into a chord of ringing overtones, and the strings you *watch* shiver are exactly the strings you *hear* ring** / a MIDI / computer-keyboard instrument that models the **tarab** (sympathetic strings) of a sarangi/sitar. **The concept:** the jury (2026-07-27) asked to get off the fragment shader and raise the bar from *dial* to *decision*. This does both — real three.js geometry (no shader surface) and an instrument where **choosing the right note IS the play**: 25 playable strings stand in front, a rack of 22 sympathetic *tarab* strings hangs behind, and a single strike radiates into everything that rings in sympathy. **The technique — modal / sympathetic-resonance coupling (`synth.ts`):** each string is a set of partials; a struck driver at `f0` radiates `k·f0`, a tarab string tuned to `fs` owns `j·fs`, and coupling is the best shared-partial coincidence weighted `1/(k·j)`: `coupling(f0,fs) = max over k,j∈1..6 of (1/(k·j))·exp(−(cents(k·f0, j·fs)/30)²)` — which reproduces the physical ordering of sympathetic resonance (**unison=1.0, octave≈0.5, fifth≈0.17, fourth≈0.08**, sub-0.06 stays dark). The driver is a **Karplus–Strong** pluck at true pitch; every above-threshold tarab string is triggered with coupling-proportional amplitude, a slow sympathetic build (attack grows as coupling falls), and up to ~6 s decay — so one key is audibly richer and longer than a dry oscillator. **The decision-stakes (and why it's NOT the banned JI net):** the tarab rack is tuned in **just intonation** (a warm Bilaval-leaning raga `1, 9/8, 5/4, 4/3, 3/2, 5/3, 15/8` × 3 octaves) while the keybed is **honest equal temperament** — `midiToHz(m)=440·2^((m−69)/12)`, **no quantizer** rounds your played pitch onto a scale. Because the two tunings *differ*, a consonant note blooms fully while an out-of-key note only shimmers: the JI/ET mismatch is turned into *musical stakes* (right note = full sympathetic bloom), the exact opposite of a snap-to-scale safety net. **The audio→geometry weld:** every tarab string is a real `THREE.Line` whose interior vertices displace along a decaying standing wave (`sin(π·u·mode)` pinned at nut+bridge × per-string shimmer), amplitude from the *same* coupling map that drives the audio — the string you watch ring is the string you hear ring. Real geometry (47 `THREE.Line` objects), UnrealBloom pass for warm glow only, not as the surface. **Input = Web MIDI** (`navigator.requestMIDIAccess`; note-on strikes the keybed at true pitch) with a **computer-keyboard fallback** (A–L white, W/E/T/Y/U black, Z/X octave) so it's playable with no device. **Output = three.js instanced line geometry** (deliberately off the 8×-in-15 WebGL2 fragment-shader monoculture the jury banned). **Named refs:** the **tarab** sympathetic strings of the **sarangi/sitar** (the physical instrument modelled) · La Monte Young, **_The Well-Tuned Piano_** (the sympathetic-resonance / JI shimmer aesthetic) · Jean-Marie Adrien, **"The missing link: modal synthesis"** (1991) (each string as a resonant mode, coupling as spectral overlap). **Subsystems (≥3):** Web MIDI / keyboard input router + the shared-partial coupling resonator bank (Karplus–Strong) + the three.js standing-wave geometry with UnrealBloom = 3+. **Degrades fully:** AudioContext opens only on the Start gesture; no MIDI → keyboard message; no WebGL → a `text-destructive` notice but the sympathetic audio + autoplay still run; a seeded **`mulberry32`** autoplay phrase drives the *exact same* `strike()` path so it self-animates and stays audible headless with no MIDI and no speakers; full teardown (rAF cancel, keydown/up + resize listeners removed, `audio.close()`, geometry/material/composer dispose). No strobe (bloom is steady glow). **Ambition — 2/5:** #2 (≥3 subsystems) · #3 (tarab / La Monte Young / Adrien 1991). **diversity:** last-10 ≈ [2952,2960,2992,3008,3040,3048,3056,3080,3120]; audit `banned` = [**voice/mic input** (~5×) · **touch input** (~4×) · **WebGL2 fragment-shader output** (8× — jury-banned) · **altered-states vibe** (8× — jury moratorium) · **JI/pentatonic input net**]; `picked` = [**MIDI/keyboard** input (a pianist's native surface; neither voice nor touch) · **three.js real 3-D geometry** output (off the banned shader) · **modal/sympathetic-resonance coupling** technique (fresh; a resonator bank, not a form-constant kit) · **warm resonant instrument** vibe with **decision-stakes** (NOT altered-states)] — clears every live ban; ET keybed, JI-tuned rack, no input quantizer (continuous-pitch protection intact). **mode:** WIDE (ledger 918 D · 920 D · 921 W · 922 D · 923 D → **924 WIDE**; jury consumed by 923 so no extend-override; three clustered DEEP voice/altered-states cycles made WIDE-with-fresh-tags the direct attack on the "too similar" flag). ONE fire, three divergent explorers. **candidates:** 3136-tarab(win — most product-relevant to Resonance's pianist core, cleanest dial→decision, cleanest off-shader dodge via real geometry, best 06:30 phone-review fitness with visible vibrating strings) · 3144-latency(banked ⭐⭐ HIGH, IDEAS §924 — the multi-user latency-as-canon; jury #5's standing gap; ambition 3/5 research-anchored; held: multi-user payoff unverifiable headless + Canvas2D softest dodge) · 3152-earshot(banked ⭐, IDEAS §924 — the binaural find-by-ear game; jury #2's named "output-is-not-a-screen" register; held: needs headphones — weak for phone review — and 2992-around held the binaural register one window earlier).
